claim: African trypanosomes possess hundreds of variant surface glycoprotein (VSG) genes.
source: African trypanosomes possess hundreds of variant surface glycoprotein ( VSG ) genes, but only one is expressed from a telomeric expression site (ES) at any given time.
evidence: This is supported by citation to established knowledge in the field (Berriman et al., 2005 is cited in the Introduction).

claim: Only one VSG gene is expressed from a telomeric expression site (ES) at any given time in trypanosomes.
source: African trypanosomes possess hundreds of variant surface glycoprotein ( VSG ) genes, but only one is expressed from a telomeric expression site (ES) at any given time.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations (Hertz-Fowler et al., 2008).

claim: Expression of a second VSG alone is sufficient to silence the active VSG gene.
source: We found that the expression of a second VSG alone is sufficient to silence the active VSG gene and directionally attenuate the ES by disruptor of telomeric silencing-1B (DOT1B)-mediated histone methylation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Expression of a second VSG directionally attenuates the ES by DOT1B-mediated histone methylation.
source: We found that the expression of a second VSG alone is sufficient to silence the active VSG gene and directionally attenuate the ES by disruptor of telomeric silencing-1B (DOT1B)-mediated histone methylation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 4 showing DOT1B dependency.

claim: Three conserved expression-site-associated genes (ESAGs) serve as signal for ES attenuation.
source: Three conserved expression-site-associated genes (ESAGs) appear to serve as signal for ES attenuation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 7 showing RNAi depletion effects.

claim: Depletion of three ESAGs causes G1-phase dormancy.
source: Their depletion causes G1-phase dormancy and reversible initiation of the slender-to-stumpy differentiation pathway.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 7 showing cell cycle analysis.

claim: Depletion of three ESAGs causes reversible initiation of the slender-to-stumpy differentiation pathway.
source: Their depletion causes G1-phase dormancy and reversible initiation of the slender-to-stumpy differentiation pathway.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 5 and 6 showing PAD1 expression and developmental competence.

claim: ES-attenuated slender bloodstream trypanosomes gain full developmental competence for transformation to the tsetse fly stage.
source: ES-attenuated slender bloodstream trypanosomes gain full developmental competence for transformation to the tsetse fly stage.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 6 showing EP1 expression and differentiation in response to cis-aconitate.

claim: Each olfactory sensory neuron expresses only one olfactory receptor (OR) from a family of ~1200 genes.
source: In the mammalian central nervous system, each olfactory sensory neuron expresses only one olfactory receptor (OR) from a family of ∼1200 genes (Buck and Axel, 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Buck and Axel, 1991.

claim: Before an OR gene is expressed, all alleles are silenced and converted to heterochromatin.
source: Before an OR gene is expressed, all alleles are silenced and converted to heterochromatin (Magklara et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Magklara et al., 2011.

claim: A limiting enzymatic activity stochastically removes heterochromatin marks from one OR allele to activate it.
source: A limiting enzymatic activity then stochastically removes the heterochromatin marks from one allele to activate it.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from the olfactory receptor field.

claim: The expressed OR protein mediates a feedback loop that inhibits removal of heterochromatin marks from all other alleles.
source: The expressed OR protein mediates a feedback loop that inhibits removal of heterochromatin marks from all other alleles, preventing their transcription (Serizawa et al., 2003; Lyons et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Serizawa et al., 2003 and Lyons et al., 2013.

claim: Plasmodium falciparum expresses only one out of 60 members of the var gene family.
source: The malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum, for example, expresses only one out of 60 members of the var gene family, each coding for different versions of the surface virulence factor PfEMP1 (Guizetti and Scherf, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Guizetti and Scherf, 2013.

claim: The trypanosome cell surface is covered with millions of copies of VSG that form a dense layer impervious to host-derived antibodies.
source: In the mammalian host, the cell surface is covered with millions of copies of VSG that form a dense layer that is virtually impervious to host-derived antibodies (Cross, 1975; Engstler et al., 2007; Schwede et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cross, 1975; Engstler et al., 2007; Schwede et al., 2011.

claim: VSGs are highly immunogenic and provoke a rapid and efficient immune response.
source: VSGs are highly immunogenic and provoke a rapid and efficient immune response that diminishes the parasite population.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the trypanosome field.

claim: Trypanosomes that switch to expression of another immunologically distinct VSG survive immune clearance.
source: Only trypanosomes that have successfully switched to expression of another, structurally similar but immunologically distinct VSG survive.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of antigenic variation.

claim: Trypanosomes possess several hundred VSG genes.
source: Trypanosomes possess several hundred VSG genes (Berriman et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Berriman et al., 2005.

claim: VSG genes are expressed from one of ~15 telomeric expression sites (ES).
source: VSG genes are expressed from one of ∼15 telomeric expression sites (ES) but only one of these is transcribed at any given time (Hertz-Fowler et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hertz-Fowler et al., 2008.

claim: Chromatin remodeling plays an important role in maintaining monoallelic expression of the active ES.
source: Chromatin remodeling appears to play an important role in maintaining the monoallelic expression of the active ES (Horn and McCulloch, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Horn and McCulloch, 2010.

claim: Antigenic variation can result from a change in the active ES through gene conversion at the VSG locus.
source: Antigenic variation can result from either a change in the active ES, usually gene conversion at the VSG locus, or by an epigenetic change that results in silencing of the active ES and transcription of a previously silent ES (in situ switch).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Antigenic variation can result from an epigenetic change that silences the active ES and transcribes a previously silent ES (in situ switch).
source: Antigenic variation can result from either a change in the active ES, usually gene conversion at the VSG locus, or by an epigenetic change that results in silencing of the active ES and transcription of a previously silent ES (in situ switch).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: No mechanism or factor has been identified that is involved in the initiation of in situ switching.
source: No mechanism or factor has been identified that is involved in the initiation of the latter.
evidence: This statement reflects the state of knowledge prior to this study.

claim: The trypanosome life cycle represents a succession of proliferative and quiescent developmental forms.
source: The complex life cycle of T. brucei represents a succession of proliferative and quiescent developmental forms, which vary widely in cell architecture and function (MacGregor et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to MacGregor et al., 2012.

claim: Throughout the parasite's life cycle, the plasma membrane is covered with a series of different surface coats.
source: Throughout the parasite's life cycle, the plasma membrane is covered with a series of different surface coats.
evidence: This is established knowledge about trypanosome biology.

claim: Antigenic variation only occurs in the mammalian host, and not in the transmitting tsetse fly.
source: Antigenic variation only occurs in the mammalian host, and not in the transmitting tsetse fly.
evidence: This is established knowledge about trypanosome biology.

claim: The trypanosome bloodstream form ES is exclusively functional in the proliferating slender bloodstream stage.
source: Consequently, the trypanosome bloodstream form ES is exclusively functional in the proliferating slender bloodstream stage of the parasite.
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that antigenic variation only occurs in the mammalian host.

claim: Trypanosomes differentiate to the quiescent stumpy form in response to quorum sensing.
source: In response to quorum sensing, the trypanosomes differentiate to the quiescent stumpy form.
evidence: This is established knowledge, supported by citation to Reuner et al., 1997.

claim: Stumpy forms are competent for the developmental transition to procyclic forms after ingestion by a tsetse fly.
source: Stumpy forms are competent for the next developmental transition to procyclic forms, which occurs after ingestion by a tsetse fly (Reuner et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Reuner et al., 1997.

claim: The developmental transition from stumpy to procyclic is accompanied by silencing of the active ES.
source: This developmental transition is accompanied by silencing of the active ES so that allelic exclusion is lost.
evidence: This is established knowledge about trypanosome development.

claim: How ES silencing during developmental transition is achieved is unknown.
source: How this silencing is achieved is unknown.
evidence: This statement reflects the state of knowledge prior to this study.

claim: High-level expression of an ectopic VSG transgene initiates directional silencing of the active ES from the telomere inwards.
source: In this study, we show that high-level expression of an ectopic VSG transgene is sufficient to initiate the directional silencing of the active ES from the telomere inwards.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figure 2.

claim: The silencing of the active ES is dependent on the histone methyltransferase DOT1B.
source: The silencing of the active ES is dependent on the histone methyltransferase DOT1B.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: The VSG itself mediates a feedback loop that controls the state of monoallelic gene expression.
source: Thus, the VSG itself mediates a feedback loop that controls the state of monoallelic gene expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing VSG-induced ES attenuation.

claim: Transcriptional activity of the ES directly determines cell proliferation via a subset of ESAGs.
source: Furthermore, we show that transcriptional activity of the ES directly determines cell proliferation and developmental competence via a subset of expression site associated genes (ESAGs).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 7.

claim: Transcriptional activity of the ES directly determines developmental competence via a subset of ESAGs.
source: Furthermore, we show that transcriptional activity of the ES directly determines cell proliferation and developmental competence via a subset of expression site associated genes (ESAGs).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 5, 6, and 7.

claim: The trypanosome ES can be regarded as a fine-tuned regulator at the crossroads of antigenic variation, proliferation, and development.
source: Thus, the trypanosome ES can be regarded as a fine-tuned regulator at the crossroads of antigenic variation, proliferation, and development.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the experimental findings.

claim: VSG121 protein was detectable within 4-6 hr after induction.
source: The VSG121 protein was detectable within 4–6 hr after induction (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: After 24 hr of VSG121 induction, the surface coat of all cells was dominated by VSG121.
source: After 24 hr, the surface coat of all cells was dominated by VSG121 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The amount of VSG221 declined to 21(±2)% after 24 hr of VSG121 induction.
source: and the amount of VSG221 had declined to 21(±2)% (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Expression of an ectopic VSG at wild-type quantities causes a reduction in the abundance of the ES-resident VSG with a half-life of 12 hr.
source: Thus, expression of an ectopic VSG at wild-type quantities caused a reduction in the abundance of the ES-resident VSG, which decreased with a half-life of 12 hr that corresponds to the population doubling time within the first 24 hr of induction.
evidence: This is supported by quantification data in Figure 1B.

claim: ESAG1 and 2 transcripts decrease faster than ESAG12 mRNA after VSG121 induction.
source: ESAG1 and 2 transcripts decrease faster than ESAG12 mRNA. After 0, 4, and 8 hr of ectopic VSG121 induction, mRNA levels of three ESAGs were quantified using 32P-labeled probes on Northern blots and normalized to 18S rRNA using a fluorescent probe.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Expression site attenuation starts at the telomere and is released in the reverse direction.
source: Expression site attenuation starts at the telomere and is released in the reverse direction.
evidence: This is supported by GFP reporter data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: VSG121 induction causes cumulative growth reduction over 9 days.
source: Cumulative growth curve after induction of ectopic VSG121 expression. Two independent clones were analyzed for 9 days in the absence (−tet) or presence (+tet) of 1 µg/ml tetracycline.
evidence: This is supported by growth curve data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: VSG121 induction causes a significant increase in 1K1N cells (G1 phase) after 24 hr.
source: Cell cycle analysis. 221ES.121tet cells were induced for VSG121 expression and fixed at the time points indicated. The configurations of the mitochondrial genome (kinetoplast, K) and the nucleus (N) were visualized by light microscopy following staining with DAPI.
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Cell cycle retardation has no effect on cell morphology.
source: Cell cycle retardation has no effect on cell morphology. Trypanosomes before (−tet) and 3 days after VSG121 induction (+tet) were stained with DAPI and the cell surface labeled using AMCA-sulfo-NHS.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Expression site attenuation leads to reduced growth, but not to cell cycle arrest.
source: Expression site attenuation leads to reduced growth, but not to cell cycle arrest. Incorporation of EdU into 221ES.121tet cells induced for VSG121 expression.
evidence: This is supported by EdU incorporation data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: RNA synthesis rate decreases to 30% after 24 and 48 hr of VSG121 induction.
source: After 8 hr of tet induction, no altered fluorescence intensity was observed. After both 24 and 48 hr, fluorescence intensity was significantly decreased to 30% (p<0.0001; unpaired t test).
evidence: This is supported by BrUTP incorporation data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Ectopic expression of VSG121 causes reduction in rDNA polymerase I-driven luciferase expression.
source: Ectopic expression of VSG121 causes reduction in gene expression. (A) Luciferase reporters were inserted downstream of an rDNA polymerase I promoter
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Ectopic expression of VSG121 causes reduction in polymerase II-driven tubulin locus luciferase expression.
source: and (B) into the polymerase II-transcribed tubulin locus.
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: DOT1B depletion prevents VSG221 protein reduction during VSG121 expression.
source: Quantification of VSG protein levels during the course of tetracycline-induced VSG121 expression in DOT1B-depleted cells. Quantification was done by normalization to the paraflagellar rod protein (PFR), using the Licor Odyssey system.
evidence: This is supported by protein quantification data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: DOT1B-depleted cells show no growth defect after VSG121 induction.
source: Growth curve after induction of ectopic VSG121 expression in a Δdot1b cell line. Two independent clones were analyzed for 25 days in the absence (−tet) or presence (+tet) of 1 µg/ml tetracycline.
evidence: This is supported by growth curve data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: ES luciferase activity decreases after VSG121 induction in wild-type cells but not in DOT1B-depleted cells.
source: A luciferase reporter gene (LUC) was inserted into the active VSG221 ES (upper panel) of Δdot1b.121tet and 221ES.121tet cells. VSG121 expression was induced in the resulting LucESΔdot1b.121tet and LucES.221ES.121tet cells and luciferase activity of three (LucESΔdot1b.121tet) or two (LucES.221ES.121tet) independent clones was measured at the time points indicated
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: GFP:PADutr and endogenous PAD1 are both expressed following ES attenuation.
source: GFP:PADutr and endogenous PAD1 are both expressed following ES attenuation. Maximum intensity projections of three-channel, 3D images (100 images, z-step: 200 nm) of GFP:PADutr.221ES.121tet cells induced for VSG121.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: PAD1 expression is limited to G1 cells.
source: PAD1 expression is limited to G1. GFP:PAD1utr is visible in more G1 cells and also in other cell cycle stages.
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis data shown in Figures 5B and 5C.

claim: At day 2 after VSG121 induction, 31.1(±0.1)% of cells show GFP:PADutr expression.
source: At day 2, 31.1(±0.1)% of the cells showed GFP expression (mean ± SD for two clones).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: ES-attenuated trypanosomes express EP1 on the cell surface after cis-aconitate treatment at 37°C.
source: Flow cytometry of EP1 surface expression at 37°C. The induced cell line 221ES.121tet was treated with cis-aconitate at 37°C in bloodstream form medium for 0, 6, and 24 hr (+tet). Non-induced cells (−tet) were used as a control.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: After 6 hr of cis-aconitate treatment at 37°C, approximately 60% of ES-attenuated cells express EP1.
source: Percentage of cells expressing EP1 at the surface in (A). Values represent mean ± SD of two independent clones.
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Cis-aconitate treatment causes cell cycle arrest in ES-attenuated cells.
source: Cell cycle analysis after treatment with cis-aconitate for various lengths of time. At least 100 cells were analyzed for each time point.
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: At 27°C, after 6 hr of cis-aconitate treatment, 58(±8)% of ES-attenuated cells show EP1 expression.
source: After 6 hr, 58(±8)% of cells revealed strong EP1 fluorescence on the cell surface, while only 5(±2)% of the control population were EP1-positive (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 6D and 6E.

claim: ES-attenuated trypanosomes accelerate the cell cycle after 24 hr of cis-aconitate treatment and start growing as procyclic trypanosomes.
source: Interestingly, the ES-attenuated trypanosomes accelerated the cell cycle after 24 hr and started growing as procyclic trypanosomes (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is supported by growth curve data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Cis-aconitate treatment releases growth attenuation in ES-attenuated cells.
source: Cis-aconitate treatment releases growth attenuation. After induction for ectopic VSG121 expression for 48 hr, 221ES.121tet cells were transferred to differentiation medium at 27°C in the presence or absence of cis-aconitate and kept at a density of 2 × 106 cells/ml.
evidence: This is supported by growth curve data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: ESAG1 RNAi causes transient growth retardation after 2 days.
source: Growth of GFP:PADutr cells induced for RNAi against either (A) ESAG1
evidence: This is supported by growth curve data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: ESAG1 RNAi induces GFP:PADutr expression.
source: Flow cytometric analysis of GFP:PADutr expression in a time course of (B) ESAG1-RNAi
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: ESAG2 RNAi causes severe growth defect after 3 days.
source: or (C) ESAG2 is presented as the cumulative mean cell number ± SD for two (ESAG1) and three (ESAG2) independent clones.
evidence: This is supported by growth curve data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: ESAG2 RNAi induces GFP:PADutr expression in 75% of cells after 3 days.
source: After 3 days, GFP was detected in 75% of all cells.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: ESAG8 depletion causes transient growth retardation and leads to appearance of GFP-positive cells at day 3.
source: In contrast, RNAi against ESAGs 8 (C) and 12 (D) leads to transient growth retardation after day 2, but only ESAG8 depletion leads to the appearance of a fraction of GFP-positive cells at day 3.
evidence: This is supported by growth curve and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Depletion of ESAGs 3 and 6/7 causes severe growth phenotypes without induction of GFP:PADutr expression.
source: Depletion of ESAGs 3 (A) and 6/7 (B) causes severe growth phenotypes without induction of GFP:PADutr expression.
evidence: This is supported by growth curve and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and 1B.

claim: Starting at day 5 of VSG121 induction, the attenuation of the VSG221 ES was gradually lifted.
source: Starting at day 5 of VSG121 induction, the attenuation of the VSG221 ES was gradually lifted.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 1B and 2C.

claim: The kinetics of ES re-activation is directional, starting at the promoter and proceeding towards the telomere.
source: Interestingly, the kinetics of ES re-activation was also directional, starting at the promoter and proceeding towards the telomere.
evidence: This is supported by GFP reporter data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: VSG221 mRNA slowly increased to pre-induction levels between days 5 and 8.
source: VSG221 mRNA slowly increased to pre-induction levels between days 5 and 8 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA quantification data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: At day 8, the VSG221 surface coat had returned and VSG121 was back to pre-induction levels.
source: At day 8, the VSG221 surface coat had returned and VSG121 was back to pre-induction levels (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by protein quantification data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: With onset of VSG ES reactivation, the G1-retardation was lifted and at day 10, the population doubling times were back to normal (6 hr).
source: With onset of VSG ES reactivation, the G1-retardation was lifted, cell cycle progression was accelerated, and at day 10, the population doubling times were back to normal (6 hr) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by growth curve data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: All 20 analyzed clonal populations re-activated the VSG221 ES with no indication of ES switching.
source: We have analyzed 20 clonal populations and all clones re-activated the VSG221 ES; no indication of ES switching was found.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations from multiple clones.

claim: More than 20% of the population was responsive to re-induction of VSG121 after 10 days without tetracycline.
source: We cultivated the trypanosomes for an additional 10 days in the absence of tetracycline and then re-induced expression of VSG121. More than 20% of the population was responsive to re-induction and showed strong VSG121 expression, pointing against destructive mutations in the inducible expression system.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: The induction of VSG121 expression resulted in the rapid decrease of VSG221 mRNA and protein.
source: The induction of VSG121 expression resulted in the rapid decrease of VSG221 mRNA and protein.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The ectopic VSG121 dominated the surface coat for several days.
source: The ectopic VSG121 dominated the surface coat for several days.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 1B and 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The ESAGs were down regulated after VSG121 induction, showing that induction of a second VSG gene attenuates the entire active ES.
source: The ESAGs were also down regulated, showing that induction of a second VSG gene attenuates the entire active ES.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The initial spike in the production of ectopic VSG acts as an immediate early signal relayed to an epigenetic ES silencing machinery that requires DOT1B.
source: Our data further indicate that the initial spike in the production of ectopic VSG acts as an immediate early signal, which is relayed to an epigenetic ES silencing machinery that requires the histone methyltransferase DOT1B.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing DOT1B dependency in Figure 4.

claim: In stable VSG double-expressors with a second VSG inserted into the active ES, both VSGs are expressed in a 50/50 ratio, not exceeding 100% compared to wild-type single expressors.
source: In these double-expressors, both VSGs are expressed in a 50/50 ratio, not exceeding a total amount of 100% compared to wild-type single expressors (data not shown).
evidence: This is based on unpublished experimental observations.

claim: High-level expression of a second VSG alone is sufficient to initiate attenuation of the active ES.
source: Thus, high-level expression of a second VSG alone is sufficient to initiate attenuation of the active ES.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The second VSG does not have to be expressed from an ES to cause ES attenuation.
source: Importantly and unlike the endogenous VSG, this second VSG does not have to be expressed from an ES and it does not need to be transcribed by RNA polymerase I.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental design using T7 promoter-driven VSG121 expression.

claim: VSG silencing and shutdown of the active ES are mechanistically distinct events.
source: Furthermore, VSG silencing and shutdown of the active ES are mechanistically distinct events, as in DOT1B-knockout trypanosomes, the ES-resident VSG is silenced upon VSG overexpression, but the ESAGs are not.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Neither the initial surplus of VSG production nor the non-trypanosomal T7 RNA polymerase system is toxic.
source: No phenotype is observed after VSG overexpression in the DOT1B-knockout cells, proving that neither the initial surplus of VSG production nor the non-trypanosomal T7 RNA polymerase system is toxic.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In the mammalian olfactory receptor system, expression of an ectopic OR transgene mediates feedback inhibition that prevents expression of the active endogenous OR gene.
source: In the mammalian olfactory receptor (OR) system, the expression of an ectopic OR transgene is sufficient to mediate a feedback inhibition that prevents the expression of the active endogenous OR gene, independent of the receptor signal transduction pathway (Nguyen et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Nguyen et al., 2007.

claim: The VSG-mediated attenuation of the trypanosome ES is strongly reminiscent of the OR feedback inhibition system.
source: This is strongly reminiscent of the VSG-mediated attenuation of the trypanosome ES reported here.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by comparing the two systems.

claim: The mechanistic principle of feedback inhibition in monoallelic expression appears to be conserved between kinetoplastids and mammals.
source: Despite the enormous evolutionary distance between kinetoplastids and mammals the mechanistic principle appears to be conserved.
evidence: This is inferred from the similarity between the OR and VSG systems.

claim: The control of monoallelic expression of VSG links antigenic variation, host range determination, and parasite development.
source: Our work suggests that the control of monoallelic expression of VSG links at least three key-processes, namely antigenic variation, host range determination, and parasite development.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the experimental findings.

claim: Any trypanosome with an attenuated ES will experience a time window of full developmental competence.
source: Any trypanosome with an attenuated ES will experience a time window of full developmental competence.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing PAD1 expression and developmental competence.

claim: The stumpy life cycle stage with its genuine cell cycle arrest can be bypassed through ES attenuation.
source: Thus, the stumpy life cycle stage with its genuine cell cycle arrest can be bypassed.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ES-attenuated cells gain developmental competence without becoming stumpy forms.

claim: The experimental system initiates VSG switching but is not suited for completion of the process because it does not provide functional ESAGs.
source: While our experimental system clearly initiates VSG switching, it is not suited for completion of the process, most likely because it does not provide functional ESAGs.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental observations.

claim: The cells react to incomplete ES switching by not fully silencing the ES, but rather attenuating its activity to about 20%.
source: Interestingly, the cells react by not fully silencing the ES, but rather attenuating its activity to about 20%, probably by chromatin remodeling after histone methylation.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 1B and 2.

claim: In response to ES attenuation, trypanosomes enter a semi-quiescent state with a specifically extended G1-phase.
source: In response to ES attenuation trypanosomes enter a semi-quiescent state with a specifically extended G1-phase.
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The parasites remain in the slow growth state for about 5 days and then resume normal growth without any sign of reduced fitness.
source: The parasites remain in this slow growth state for about 5 days and then resume normal growth without any sign of reduced fitness.
evidence: This is supported by growth curve data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: ES attenuation is triggered by the brief period of true VSG overexpression.
source: While ES attenuation is triggered by the brief period of true VSG overexpression, the entry into the dormant phase is the consequence of ESAG shortage.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: The entry into the dormant phase is the consequence of ESAG shortage.
source: While ES attenuation is triggered by the brief period of true VSG overexpression, the entry into the dormant phase is the consequence of ESAG shortage.
evidence: This is inferred from the ESAG RNAi experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: ES attenuation does not lead to complete ESAG exhaustion, but rather to gradual reduction in expression.
source: It is important to note that ES attenuation does not lead to complete ESAG exhaustion, but rather to gradual reduction in expression.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Individual ESAGs could reach growth-limiting levels at different concentrations and induce G1-retardation at different times.
source: Thus, individual ESAGs could reach growth-limiting levels at different concentrations and hence, could induce G1-retardation at different times.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that different ESAGs have different kinetics of down-regulation.

claim: Depletion of ESAG1 mRNA by RNAi leads to transient growth retardation after 48 hr.
source: In fact, depletion of ESAG1 mRNA by RNAi leads to transient growth retardation after 48 hr.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Cells recover from ESAG1 depletion phenotype 2 days later, which is in agreement with the existence of ESAG1 knockout lines.
source: The cells recover from this phenotype 2 days later, which is in agreement with the existence of ESAG1 knockout lines (Carruthers et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 7A and citation to Carruthers et al., 1996.

claim: Depletion of the non-essential and ES-specific ESAG8 becomes growth limiting for a transient period.
source: Importantly, even depletion of the non-essential and ES-specific ESAG8 (Hoek and Cross, 2001) becomes growth limiting for a transient period.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C and citation to Hoek and Cross, 2001.

claim: ESAG2-RNAi is irreversibly lethal.
source: In contrast, ESAG2-RNAi is irreversibly lethal
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: A complete ES shutdown without functional rescue from non-ES copies or a new ES would be detrimental.
source: and therefore, a complete ES shutdown without functional rescue from non-ES copies or a new ES would be detrimental.
evidence: This is inferred from the lethality of ESAG2 RNAi.

claim: The down-regulation of ESAG2 to the level prevailing in ES-attenuated cells (20%) is tolerated.
source: Although essential, the down-regulation of ESAG2 to the level prevailing in ES-attenuated cells (20%) is tolerated.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ES-attenuated cells survive despite reduced ESAG2 levels.

claim: ESAG1 and 2 are N-glycosylated, membrane-associated proteins localized in the flagellar pocket.
source: ESAG1 and 2 are N-glycosylated, membrane-associated proteins localized in the flagellar pocket.
evidence: This is established knowledge, supported by citations to Nolan et al., 1999 and Pays et al., 2001.

claim: ESAG1 and 2 could function in the endosome pathway.
source: It is suggested that both could function in the endosome pathway (Nolan et al., 1999; Pays et al., 2001).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citations.

claim: ESAG1 and 2 could act in concert, which would explain the in parts redundant RNAi phenotypes.
source: Thus, ESAG1 and 2 could act in concert, which would explain the in parts redundant RNAi phenotypes.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed RNAi phenotypes.

claim: ESAG8 is found in the nucleolus and the cytoplasm, and interacts with a Puf family member.
source: In contrast, ESAG8 is found in the nucleolus and the cytoplasm, and interacts with a Puf family member (Hoek et al., 2000; Hoek et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hoek et al., 2000 and Hoek et al., 2002.

claim: ESAG8 plays a role in mRNA regulation and might be linked to the differentiation pathway.
source: This suggests that ESAG8 plays a role in mRNA regulation and might be linked to the differentiation pathway.
evidence: This is speculation based on the known properties of ESAG8.

claim: The concept of transient ES attenuation rather than immediate and complete ES silencing may be of physiological relevance.
source: Thus, the concept of transient ES attenuation rather than immediate and complete ES silencing may be of some physiological relevance
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Transient ES attenuation could allow probing for ES performance, including ESAG functionality, VSG switching orders, quality of novel mosaic VSGs, or newly assembled expression sites.
source: it could allow probing for ES performance, for example ESAG functionality, VSG switching orders, quality of novel mosaic VSGs, or newly assembled expression sites.
evidence: This is speculation about the potential biological function of ES attenuation.

claim: If both VSGs are compatible and produce a mixed and dense surface coat and the ESAGs of the new ES are fully functional, the old expression site is rapidly and completely silenced with no effects on cell cycle progression.
source: If both VSGs are compatible, and produce a mixed and dense surface coat and the ESAGs of the new ES are fully functional, the old expression site is rapidly and completely silenced with no effects on cell cycle progression.
evidence: This is speculation about what happens during successful ES switching.

claim: If any component of the new ES fails or is not sufficiently functional, the cells can adjust growth to very basal levels.
source: However, if any component of the new ES fails or is not sufficiently functional, the cells can adjust growth, in the extreme, to very basal levels.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed growth phenotypes.

claim: Parasites may gain time to adapt to new conditions or reverse the attenuation and re-activate the old ES.
source: This way the parasites may either gain time to adapt to the new conditions or reverse the attenuation and re-activate the old ES.
evidence: This is speculation about the biological function of reversible ES attenuation.

claim: An unsuccessful switching event would escape experimental detection.
source: We suggest that the latter case resembles an unsuccessful switching event, which would escape experimental detection.
evidence: This is speculation about why unsuccessful switches are not observed.

claim: We can only observe successful VSG switching events, thereby neglecting the capacity of trypanosomes to reverse switching directions.
source: In fact, we can only observe successful VSG switching events, thereby neglecting the surprising capacity of trypanosomes to reverse switching directions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: ES switching plasticity could become particularly productive in varying host environments.
source: This flexibility could become particularly productive in varying host environments.
evidence: This is speculation about the biological significance of ES switching flexibility.

claim: Provided a sufficiently high ES activation frequency exists, the parasites could effectively probe for host serum-compatible ESAGs.
source: Provided a sufficiently high ES activation frequency exists, the parasites could effectively probe for host serum-compatible ESAGs (Bitter et al., 1998; Chaves et al., 1999; Pays et al., 2001).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citations.

claim: ES switching plasticity could determine the host range.
source: Hence, ES switching plasticity could determine the host range.
evidence: This is speculation based on the role of ESAGs in host compatibility.

claim: Trypanosoma b. rhodesiense is human-infective and thought to be a host-range variant of T. b. brucei.
source: One extreme example for this is Trypanosoma b. rhodesiense, which is human-infective and thought to be a host-range variant of T. b. brucei.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: T. b. rhodesiense parasites are specifically adapted to human serum by expression of the serum-resistance antigen (SRA) from one particular VSG ES in most isolates.
source: The parasites are specifically adapted to human serum by expression of the serum-resistance antigen (SRA) from one particular VSG ES in most isolates.
evidence: This is established knowledge about T. b. rhodesiense.

claim: The structure of the SRA-containing ES is unusual as it is missing several ESAGs present in all other ESs.
source: The structure of the SRA-containing ES is unusual as it is missing several ESAGs present in all other ESs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the SRA-containing ES.

claim: During an infection of a human, an in situ switch to a VSG in another ES would cause loss of SRA expression, with lethal consequences for T. b. rhodesiense.
source: During an infection of a human, an in situ switch to a VSG in another ES would cause loss of SRA expression, with lethal consequences.
evidence: This is inference based on the requirement for SRA in human serum resistance.

claim: T. b. rhodesiense must not switch off the SRA-containing ES, thus making the ESAG-dependent differentiation pathway obsolete.
source: Thus, T. b. rhodesiense must not switch off the SRA-containing ES, thus making the ESAG-dependent differentiation pathway obsolete.
evidence: This is inference based on the requirement to maintain SRA expression.

claim: The T. b. rhodesiense ES has lost ESAG1, 2 and 8 because the ESAG-dependent differentiation pathway is obsolete.
source: This may be the reason why the T. b. rhodesiense ES has lost ESAG1, 2 and 8.
evidence: This is speculation about the evolutionary reason for ESAG loss.

claim: ES attenuation causes growth retardation, which could become mechanistically relevant during differentiation to the stumpy stage.
source: The fact that ES attenuation causes growth retardation could also become mechanistically relevant during another phase of the trypanosome life cycle, namely upon differentiation to the G1/G0-arrested stumpy stage.
evidence: This is speculation about the relevance of ES attenuation to stumpy formation.

claim: The developmental transition from slender to stumpy bloodstream stage is initiated by quorum sensing of the trypanosome-derived compound SIF.
source: The developmental transition from the proliferating slender to the quiescent stumpy bloodstream stage is initiated by quorum sensing of the trypanosome-derived compound SIF (Reuner et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Reuner et al., 1997.

claim: The monomorphic cells used in this study are unresponsive to SIF and should have lost the capacity to differentiate to the tsetse-infective stage.
source: The monomorphic cells used in this study are unresponsive to SIF and hence, should have lost the capacity to differentiate to the tsetse-infective stage (Vassella et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Vassella et al., 1997.

claim: VSG-induced ES attenuation renders monomorphic trypanosomes fully competent for development.
source: In our experiments, however, VSG-induced ES attenuation renders monomorphic trypanosomes fully competent for development.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: After 2 days of VSG overexpression, the stumpy stage marker PAD1 was strongly up-regulated, specifically in G1-phase cells.
source: After 2 days of VSG overexpression the stumpy stage marker PAD1 was strongly up-regulated, specifically in G1-phase cells, and despite global transcriptional silencing being initiated at the same time.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 5B and 5C.

claim: PAD1 up-regulation indicates a highly specific event orchestrated solely by the state of the VSG expression site in the absence of SIF.
source: This indicates a highly specific event, which, in the absence of SIF, is orchestrated solely by the state of the VSG expression site.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that PAD1 is induced without SIF.

claim: The induced expression of a second VSG leads to the formation of stumpy forms in a pleomorphic strain.
source: We are currently investigating this alternative pathway in a pleomorphic strain. The induced expression of a second VSG indeed leads to the formation of stumpy forms (data not shown).
evidence: This is based on unpublished experimental observations.

claim: VSG itself is not involved in signaling ES attenuation, as it is not limiting in the experimental system.
source: While VSG itself is not involved, as it is not limiting in our system, three ESAGs signal ES attenuation to the differentiation pathway.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental design where total VSG levels remain constant.

claim: Three ESAGs signal ES attenuation to the differentiation pathway.
source: While VSG itself is not involved, as it is not limiting in our system, three ESAGs signal ES attenuation to the differentiation pathway.
evidence: This is supported by RNAi data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Depletion of ESAGs 1, 2 and 8 mRNA by RNAi resulted in induction of the PAD1 reporter GFP:PADutr.
source: Depletion of ESAGs 1, 2 and 8 mRNA by RNAi resulted in induction of the PAD1 reporter GFP:PADutr.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Down-regulation of ESAGs other than 1, 2, and 8 did not cause GFP:PADutr expression.
source: Down-regulation of any of the other ESAGs did not cause GFP:PADutr expression.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The specificity of the pathway suggests that ES activity controls the induction of transient developmental competence.
source: This underlines the specificity of the pathway and suggests that ES activity controls the induction of transient developmental competence.
evidence: This is inferred from the specific effects of ESAGs 1, 2, and 8 depletion.

claim: By embedding the endogenous PAD1 protein into the VSG coat, the ES attenuated trypanosomes became fully responsive to the developmental trigger cis-aconitate.
source: Remarkably, by embedding the endogenous PAD1 protein into the VSG coat, the ES attenuated trypanosomes became fully responsive to the developmental trigger cis-aconitate.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: ES-attenuated trypanosomes initiated transformation to the procyclic insect stage with the same kinetics as stumpy parasites.
source: They initiated transformation to the procyclic insect stage with the same kinetics as stumpy parasites.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: SIF-mediated stumpy formation differs from ES-regulated cell dormancy in that stumpy parasites are terminally differentiated.
source: There is, however, one principal feature that distinguishes SIF-mediated stumpy formation from ES-regulated cell dormancy. While stumpy parasites are terminally differentiated and can only survive if taken up by an insect, the onset of differentiation is fully reversible in the ES-attenuated trypanosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations showing reversibility of ES attenuation.

claim: The onset of differentiation is fully reversible in ES-attenuated trypanosomes.
source: While stumpy parasites are terminally differentiated and can only survive if taken up by an insect, the onset of differentiation is fully reversible in the ES-attenuated trypanosomes.
evidence: This is supported by data showing ES re-activation in Figures 1B, 2C, and 3A.

claim: ES-attenuated parasites linger in an intermediate state with open developmental choices.
source: We postulate that these parasites linger in an intermediate state with open developmental choices
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed reversibility and developmental competence.

claim: ES attenuation opens a time-window in which trypanosomes can progress in two directions: either by differentiating to the insect stage or by returning to proliferation in the mammalian host.
source: Thus, ES attenuation opens a time-window in which the trypanosomes linger in an intermediate state and can progress in two directions, either by differentiating to the insect stage or by returning to proliferation in the mammalian host.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations of reversibility and developmental competence.

claim: The observation that ES attenuation is reversible questions the common view that trypanosome development is inevitably unidirectional.
source: This questions the common view that trypanosome development is inevitably unidirectional as in the case of the SIF-induced pathway (MacGregor et al., 2011).
evidence: This is inference based on the experimental findings and citation to MacGregor et al., 2011.

claim: ES attenuation flexibility could become biologically relevant during early infections when certain ESAGs or VSGs are not compatible with the new host environment.
source: This high flexibility might become biologically relevant especially during early infections, when certain ESAGs or VSGs are not compatible with the new host environment: cells either adapt or regain fly-infectivity.
evidence: This is speculation about the biological significance of ES attenuation.

claim: The state of the expression site must not be regarded as a simple on-off switch, but rather represents a fine-tuned module at the crossroads of antigenic variation and development.
source: Thus, the state of the expression site must not be regarded as a simple on-off switch, but rather represents a fine-tuned module at the unexpected crossroads of antigenic variation and development.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from all the experimental findings.

claim: All cell lines generated in this study are based on T. brucei 427 MITat 1.2 13-90 bloodstream forms (221ES).
source: All cell lines generated in this study are based on T. brucei 427 MITat 1.2 13-90 bloodstream forms (221ES) (Wirtz et al., 1999)
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by citation.

claim: Cells were cultivated in HMI-9 medium with 10% fetal bovine serum at 37°C and 5% CO2.
source: and were cultivated in HMI-9 medium with 10% fetal bovine serum (Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO) at 37°C and 5% CO2.
evidence: This is a methodological statement.
